content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_6feda53b2382c63bf47b25\", \"title\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\", \"name\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\", \"revisionId\": \"a7f6f837df\", \"createdTime\": \"2026-02-12T23:52:18Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2026-02-13T00:41:06Z\", \"text\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\\nAngels will ask what each bet cost and what it brought in. This is how we count it so the three of us say the same thing. It replaces the quick plan I left on our board.\\nGo by the bank. SVB\\u2019s Payment Processed notices are the one place I know with a line per payment, and what the banks say is our ground source of truth. Start at the first SVB wires in Sep 2023 and stop at the last run on Feb 2. Anything paid out of Chase isn\\u2019t in here.\\nWhat counts is money that left the company and stayed out. A notice is where you start, not the last word. Take a notice as paid unless one of us has said the money came back. If someone we paid closes out their file with us and tells us what they received, that beats the notices for them. Money we moved between our own accounts isn\\u2019t spending, no bucket for that. Every payee keeps its line, even at zero.\\nIf we paid a contractor some other way, it goes in only if a receipt for it reached your mail, at the amount sent, not the fee.\\nBuckets. Build is the team on Deel plus the studios and freelancers who made the games. Everything on Deel counts as team, don\\u2019t try to split it. Marketing is anything made or bought to get installs (ad networks, agencies, ad creative, playables, trailers): list it under its bet by date like the rest, but keep it out of build cost, I have those numbers. Company is legal, tools, the website, equipment and anything else that wasn\\u2019t for one of the three games: that goes in the Company column. Our own pay and anyone on Gusto aren\\u2019t in here.\\nWhich bet. Go by the Transaction Date on the notice, the whole payment to one bet: Domino Delights up to Jan 8, 2025, ZM from Jan 9, 2025 to Nov 23, 2025, Combo Fighter from Nov 24, 2025. Don\\u2019t try to work out who was on what, that\\u2019s where we\\u2019d start arguing.\\nAnything not paid in dollars stays in its own currency next to the line. Don\\u2019t add it to a dollar total.\\nWhat each game brought in is its lifetime revenue from the warehouse\\u2019s daily revenue table, as recorded. Leave Combo Fighter\\u2019s revenue off for now, on the page, on the deck and when you tell me, until we\\u2019ve checked its first sales.\\nOn the Linear project: move each payee\\u2019s issue to Done once its line is right. If your figure isn\\u2019t what the notices add up to, say why on the issue first.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_6feda53b2382c63bf47b25", "title": "Angel note: how to count the money", "name": "Angel note: how to count the money", "revisionId": "a7f6f837df", "createdTime": "2026-02-12T23:52:18Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-13T00:41:06Z", "text": "Angel note: how to count the money
Angels will ask what each bet cost and what it brought in. This is how we count it so the three of us say the same thing. It replaces the quick plan I left on our board.
Go by the bank. SVB’s Payment Processed notices are the one place I know with a line per payment, and what the banks say is our ground source of truth. Start at the first SVB wires in Sep 2023 and stop at the last run on Feb 2. Anything paid out of Chase isn’t in here.
What counts is money that left the company and stayed out. A notice is where you start, not the last word. Take a notice as paid unless one of us has said the money came back. If someone we paid closes out their file with us and tells us what they received, that beats the notices for them. Money we moved between our own accounts isn’t spending, no bucket for that. Every payee keeps its line, even at zero.
If we paid a contractor some other way, it goes in only if a receipt for it reached your mail, at the amount sent, not the fee.
Buckets. Build is the team on Deel plus the studios and freelancers who made the games. Everything on Deel counts as team, don’t try to split it. Marketing is anything made or bought to get installs (ad networks, agencies, ad creative, playables, trailers): list it under its bet by date like the rest, but keep it out of build cost, I have those numbers. Company is legal, tools, the website, equipment and anything else that wasn’t for one of the three games: that goes in the Company column. Our own pay and anyone on Gusto aren’t in here.
Which bet. Go by the Transaction Date on the notice, the whole payment to one bet: Domino Delights up to Jan 8, 2025, ZM from Jan 9, 2025 to Nov 23, 2025, Combo Fighter from Nov 24, 2025. Don’t try to work out who was on what, that’s where we’d start arguing.
Anything not paid in dollars stays in its own currency next to the line. Don’t add it to a dollar total.
What each game brought in is its lifetime revenue from the warehouse’s daily revenue table, as recorded. Leave Combo Fighter’s revenue off for now, on the page, on the deck and when you tell me, until we’ve checked its first sales.
On the Linear project: move each payee’s issue to Done once its line is right. If your figure isn’t what the notices add up to, say why on the issue first.
"}

import json,re
d=json.load(open('/tmp/svb_parsed.json'))
from collections import Counter
print(Counter(v['subject'] for v in d.values()))
rows=[]
for k,v in d.items():
    if 'Payment Processed' not in v['subject']: continue
    b=v['body']
    m=re.search(r'To: (.*?) \*\*\*(\d{4})Amount: ([\d,\.]+) ([A-Z]{3})Transaction Date: (\w{3} \d{2} \d{4})',b)
    if not m: print('NOMATCH',b[:300]); continue
    rows.append(dict(id=k,to=m.group(1),acct=m.group(2),amt=float(m.group(3).replace(',','')),ccy=m.group(4),date=m.group(5),frm=re.search(r'From: (.*?)To:',b).group(1)))
json.dump(rows,open('/tmp/rows.json','w'))
print(len(rows))
EOF

Here are your two clean paths:
Option A — Firebase Authentication (fastest)
• What lovable can do:
    ◦ Build a `/login` page with a *“Continue with Google”* button.
    ◦ Initialize Firebase (copy/paste your `apiKey`, `authDomain`).
    ◦ Call `signInWithPopup`/`signInWithRedirect` (Google provider).
    ◦ Store the Firebase ID token locally and gate routes.
• What you must do:
    ◦ Create a Firebase project, enable *Google* provider.
    ◦ Paste your Firebase config into lovable.
    ◦ (Recommended) Add a tiny backend (Node/Cloud Function) using *Firebase Admin* to *verify the ID token* and mint an *httpOnly session cookie* for your domain.
    ◦ If you want company-only access, enforce *email domain allowlist* (e.g., `@Harmony Games`) on the backend (check Token’s `email`).
Option B — Google Identity Services (pure Google OAuth)
• What lovable can do:
    ◦ Render the Google Sign-In button / One Tap.
    ◦ Use the *GIS Token Client* for `openid email profile` and receive an *ID token*.
    ◦ Pass that ID token to your backend.
• What you must do:
    ◦ Create a Google Cloud *OAuth Client ID (Web)*.
    ◦ Add *Authorized JavaScript origins* (e.g., `<http://localhost:5173>`, `<https://engine.Harmony Games>`) and *Redirect URIs* (if using redirect flow).
    ◦ Backend endpoint to *verify the ID token* (use Google libraries), create a *signed session cookie* (httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax), and return it.
    ◦ (Optional) Enforce Workspace domain by checking the token’s `hd` claim or email domain.
Which should you pick?
• *Need it working today with minimal backend?* Use *Firebase Auth* (Option A).
• *Already have your own backend and want full control?* Use *GIS (Option B)*.
lovable-ready instructions (paste)
• *Create `/login` page* with a “Continue with Google” button.
• *Auth mode toggle* in settings: `authProvider = "Firebase" | "gis"`.
• If `Firebase`:
    ◦ Config fields: `apiKey`, `authDomain`, `projectId`, etc.
    ◦ On success, show user avatar/email in header; write ID token to memory.
    ◦ Call `POST /auth/session` with the Firebase ID token; expect httpOnly session cookie.
• If `gis`:
    ◦ Config fields: `googleClientId`, `redirectUri?`.
    ◦ Render Google button; on credential response, call `POST /auth/session` with ID token; expect httpOnly session cookie.
• *Route guards*:
    ◦ Protect all editor routes; redirect unauthenticated users to `/login`.
    ◦ Show “Sign out” in the profile menu (clears cookie via `POST /auth/logout`).
• *Security*:
    ◦ Do NOT store raw tokens in `localStorage`; use *httpOnly cookies* for sessions.
    ◦ CORS: allow `<https://engine.Harmony Games>` and `<http://localhost:5173>`.
    ◦ Cookies: `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, domain = `.<http://harmonygames|Harmony Games>`.
Minimal backend you’ll need (either option)
• `POST /auth/session` — accepts an *ID token*, verifies it, issues an *httpOnly session cookie*.
• `GET /me` — returns user profile from the session.
• `POST /auth/logout` — clears the cookie.
• Optional: enforce *email domain allowlist*, role mapping, and audit login events.

And if this game doesn't have a high enough strategy ceiling, then it will just be a bunch of people who have hit the strategy ceiling component of the game, and then when it comes down to the wire, it's still a competition of reflexes. So in the end, it will be those with _perfect_ strategy and _fastest_ reflex that's gonna win them the game, so we're back to just competing on reflexes.

The only way you can get around that is to create a game that basically have virtually unlimited strategy ceiling, and in the history of gaming, There just isn't that many games that are like that. A few that arguably has such ceiling are games like:

Starcraft - Even when it comes to the world's best players, There is still something they can improve in their game. But many would argue the ceiling There is usually not "strategy", but the ability to manage all your Units (So more of a reflex/APM issue)

Poker - You are playing the odds, but in the end everyone knows the odds, so you're playing the other players, not really the game. Marvel Snap actually replicated these decision dilemma quite well. import json
from collections import defaultdict
rows=json.load(open('/tmp/rows.json'))
def bet(dt): return 'DD' if dt<='2025-01-08' else ('ZM' if dt<='2025-11-23' else 'CF')
by=defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float)); cnt=defaultdict(int)
for r in rows:

    by[r['acct']][bet(r['dt'])]+=r['amt']; cnt[r['acct']]+=1
for a in by: print(a, dict(by[a]), round(sum(by[a].values()),2))
EOF

input.message:
<@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID> money page is done. I counted it the way your doc says. Sheet is in my Drive and shared with you and Blake: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1YbJlGf8pr4X0ZAXLRJmnaSYLzChIjazByjMwpWrN-m8/edit

**What each bet cost to build** (Deel team plus studios and freelancers; marketing and company costs left out)
• Domino Delights: **$951,818**
• ZM: **$544,433**
• Combo Fighter: **$72,686**

**What each brought in** (lifetime, from the warehouse daily revenue table as recorded)
• Domino Delights: **$12,331**
• ZM: **$12**
• Combo Fighter: left off, as you asked

**Changes to the draft deck**
• Build cost slide: DD $985K → **$952K**, ZM $609K → **$544K**, CF $74K → **$73K**
• "What each brought in": fill in DD **$12.3K**, ZM **$12**, and leave CF off for now

**Why the build numbers are lower than your quick pass**
• Your quick pass counted marketing under each bet. Now listed but not in build cost: ZM $56,537 (Adjoe, AppLovin, PlayableX, Telegram UA) and CF $1,000 (Telegram UA)

content.text:
I built the money page, shared it with Leonard and Blake, closed out the Payee history project in Linear, and replied to Leonard in #winddown. That reply had a wrong figure for company costs, so I posted a correction under it.

**What each bet cost to build** (the team on Deel plus the studios and freelancers; marketing and company costs left out)

| | Cost to build | Brought in (lifetime, from the warehouse) |
|---|---|---|
| Domino Delights | $951,818 | $12,331 |
| ZM | $544,433 | $12 |
| Combo Fighter | $72,686 | left off until its first sales are checked, as Leonard asked |

**Changes for the draft deck:** DD goes from $985K to $952K, ZM from $609K to $544K, and CF from $74K to $73K. "What each brought in" becomes DD $12.3K and ZM $12, with CF left off.

**Why the build numbers are lower than Leonard's quick pass:**
- **Moved out of build cost:**
  - Marketing (Adjoe, AppLovin, the playable ad, the Telegram ads contractor) is still listed under each bet: $56,537 for ZM and $1,000 for CF.
  - Company costs now have their own column: $58,204 from the DD period and $7,850 from ZM.
  - Martin's laptop was paid in Bulgarian lev, so it stays as BGN 1,999 and isn't added to any dollar total.
- **Leapblock:** their accountant posted a closeout in Slack saying they received $407,944 over 30 wires. One of those, $33,290 on Sep 13, 2023, has no SVB notice. Leonard's rules say a payee's own closeout beats the notices, so DD goes up $33,290.
- **Taken out:**
  - The Apr 2024 MotMot wire of $4,032 bounced and was re-sent, so it counts once.
  - The $4,000 to JPMorgan was Blake moving money to our own Chase account; he confirmed it by email on Feb 13.
  - Oleg's $125 wire came back the same day. No receipt for the Payoneer re-send ever reached your mail (only Payoneer payment requests), so his line is $0.

All of my figures tie back exactly to Leonard's quick-pass totals.

**Linear:** all 22 payee issues are Done. The four where my number differs from the notices (Leapblock, MotMot, Oleg, JPMorgan) each have a comment explaining why, posted before I closed them.

**Correction:** in the #winddown reply I first gave the company costs as $47.1K for DD and $6.75K for ZM. The correct figures are $58,204 and $7,850, and the sheet always had those. My correction under the reply shows how the DD number adds up.

**One judgment call to check:** the $16,428.57 paid on Jan 2, 2025 to the payee whose name is redacted as "PERSON_4419_NAME LLC" is under Company. The only note anywhere is "one payment when we closed the account," and nothing ties it to a game. I told Leonard to say so if he remembers it differently.

Sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1YbJlGf8pr4X0ZAXLRJmnaSYLzChIjazByjMwpWrN-m8/edit
